title: 2026-11-05_BlackTech_PLEAD_Backdoor_Investigation_634
description: Investigate a compromised host within your network that shows signs of PLEAD infection.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The BlackTech threat group has been linked to cyber espionage campaigns targeting various organizations. Their malware, known as PLEAD, is a backdoor that establishes command and control (C2) communication, performs lateral movement, and exfiltrates data. Your task is to investigate a compromised host within your network that shows signs of PLEAD infection.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. **List all services**: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services on the host.
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

2. **Filter running services**: Narrow down the list to only running services.
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
```

3. **Inspect service details**: Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious services. Pay attention to their descriptions and paths.
   ```
systemctl cat <service>
```

4. **Identify the suspicious service**: Based on the descriptions and paths, identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. **Inspect the suspicious service**: Use the `systemctl cat` command to inspect the details of the suspicious service identified in the previous task.
   ```
systemctl cat <service>
```

2. **Identify the port**: Look for the port number in the service configuration, typically specified in the `ExecStart` line.
   ```
systemctl cat <service>
```

3. **Verify the port**: Use the `ss` command to verify that the port is being listened on.
   ```
ss -tulnp
```

levels.title: Suspicious Data Collection Service Discovery
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. **List all services**: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services on the host.
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

2. **List all timers**: Use the `systemctl` command to list all timers on the host.
   ```
systemctl list-timers --all
```

3. **Inspect timer details**: Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timers. Pay attention to their descriptions and paths.
   ```
systemctl cat <timer>
```

4. **Identify the suspicious service**: Based on the descriptions and paths, identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
   ```
systemctl cat <service>
```
